hero.filename: Shahbag Projonmo Square Uprising Demanding Capital Punishment of the War Criminals of 1971 in Bangladesh.jpg
hero.caption:
Uprising of people at Shahbag, Dhaka, Bangladesh demanding death penalty of Kader Molla and all other war criminals who are now being tried before the International Crimes Tribunal Bangladesh for the serious crimes they have committed during the Liberation War of Bangladesh in 1971. Perpetrators of war crimes, genocide and crimes against humanity have NO place in Bangladesh. This is public opinion.
BACKGROUND: On 5 February 2013, International Crimes Tribunal-2 delivered judgment against Kader Molla, who was accused of rape of minor and at least 350 murders. Tried for his crimes against humanity, his crimes were proven beyond reasonable doubt, according to the judgment. However, the Tribunal comprising of Mr Shahinur Islam, Obaidul Hasan Shahin and Mojibur Rahman awarded Kader Molla life sentence, instead of death penalty which the accused deserved. People, rejecting this lenient sentence, has risen, in Dhaka and other cities in Bangladesh.

images.filename: Shahbag Projonmo Square Uprising Demanding Death Penalty of the War Criminals of 1971 in Bangladesh 25.jpg
images.caption: Protesters at Shahbag, Dhaka, Bangladesh demanding the death penalty for Kader Molla and all other war criminals who are currently being tried before the International Crimes Tribunal Bangladesh for the war crimes they committed during the Liberation War of Bangladesh in 1971. According to the judgment, his crimes against humanity were proven beyond reasonable doubt. Many people in Dhaka and other cities in Bangladesh have rejected the perceived leniency of the sentence.

images.caption: The picture was captured during a demonstration in Shahbag square of Dhaka, Bangladesh. The demonstration was demanding for capital punishment of the criminals who committed crimes like murder, rape, firing houses, etc. during the liberation war of Bangladesh. It was initiated when the International Crime Tribunal sentenced Kader Molla to life prison, instead of death, although five out of six convictions against him were proved "beyond reasonable doubt" in the tribunal.
